title: Stellar powerhouses in the Eagle Nebula
caption: The young star cluster NGC 6611 in the Eagle Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6611 · constellation Serpens Cauda · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Dazzling stars scattered across a section of the Eagle Nebula make up NGC 6611 in this Hubble image, with dark patches punctuating the stellar landscape. NGC 6611 is an open star cluster about 6500 light-years from Earth, whose stars formed about 5.5 million years ago.

It is a very young cluster, full of hot blue stars whose fierce ultraviolet light makes the surrounding nebula glow. Astronomers call places like this HII regions, after the ionized hydrogen that makes up most of them. In the far future the region will disperse, helped along by shock waves from supernovae as its more massive young stars end their short lives.

The dark patches are not empty. They are very dense clouds of gas and dust that block light, and many may hide the early stages of star formation, before young stars clear their surroundings and emerge into view.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.20 x 3.43 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 6.1 × 6.5 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using two near-infrared filters, with F775W shown in blue, F850LP in red and subtle extra color from a ground-based image.
understand.eye: Both Hubble filters record light at or beyond the red limit of human vision, so the colors here are a translation rather than what the eye would see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture used an unusual pairing of two near-infrared filters, each exposed for 2000 seconds, and a ground-based image through more standard filters added a subtle touch of color. The frame spans about 3.2 arcminutes. From a dark site, huge dark nebulae can be seen against the Milky Way with the naked eye.
alt: Bright stars of a young cluster scattered across part of a nebula, with dark patches of dust among them.
